mainTopic: Teachings on Torah learning from תהלים, wages for building idols, and a new משנה on idol jewelry and selling attached things to gentiles
overview: This amud first finishes explaining the פסוקים of תהלים פרק א about the person who learns Torah. רבי תנחום בר חנילאי reads 'פלגי מים' as 'dividing' and says each day's learning should be split among מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד. רבא teaches that learning must lead to action. רב warns against ruling on הלכה too early and against refusing to rule once qualified, and the גמרא sets the usual age at forty. More teachings on the same פסוק follow: even the everyday talk of תלמידי חכמים is worth studying, and one who is busy with Torah succeeds, with proof from the תורה, נביאים, and כתובים. רבי אלכסנדרי then 'sells life' by teaching that one must guard one's tongue and also do good, which means learning Torah. The גמרא returns to the משנה: if a Jew built the dome where idols are placed, his wages are permitted, because an idol only becomes one at the final stroke and wages build up throughout the job. A new משנה forbids making jewelry for idols and selling attached things to gentiles, and the גמרא begins asking for the source, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the earlier point: so the versions do not get mixed up
steps.stepSummary: The last words of an earlier statement: learning from one רבי keeps a student from getting different versions of the same teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: …so that the versions will not differ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence from just before this section. Learning from one main רבי is better because the student will not end up with clashing versions of the same teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said that the basic wording of the teachings (גמרא) should be learned from one רבי, while reasoning (סברא) can be gained from many. These words give the reason for the first part: one teacher means one clear version. Different teachers may phrase the same idea differently, and that can confuse a student.

phrases.english: so that the versions will not differ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the reasoning of a statement that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Learning from one main רבי gives a student one clear version of the teaching.

steps.title: Divide your learning into three parts
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי reads 'פלגי מים' as dividing, and teaches that a person should split his learning into thirds: מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'By streams of water.' רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said: A person should always divide his years into three: one third for מקרא, one third for משנה, one third for תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק, 'על פלגי מים'. רבי תנחום בר חנילאי says this teaches that a person should split his learning into three equal parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'פלגי' (streams) shares a root with 'dividing'. So the פסוק hints that the Torah learner divides his time: תנ״ך (מקרא), משנה, and תלמוד (understanding the reasons behind the משנה). Each kind of learning gets an equal share.

keyTerms.meaning: streams of water; here read as 'dividing'
the משנה, the basic oral teachings
the analysis and reasoning behind the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known guide for a balanced learning schedule, so that no part of Torah is left out.

phrases.english: "By streams of water."
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:3. 'פלגי' can also mean 'divisions,' and the next line builds on that.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai said:
A person should always divide his years into three:
a third for Bible, a third for Mishnah,
a third for Talmud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי: לְעוֹלָם יְשַׁלֵּשׁ אָדָם שְׁנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק in תהלים and opens a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should split his Torah learning equally among מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד.

steps.title: Nobody knows how long he will live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can someone divide his years into thirds if he does not know how many years he has?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a person know how long he will live?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי תנחום's wording. You can only split your years into thirds if you know how many years you have, and nobody knows that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'divide his years' sounds like spending the first third of life on מקרא, the next on משנה, and the last on תלמוד. That plan cannot work, because no one knows where his life's 'thirds' fall. The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge to the wording.

phrases.english: Does a person know how long he will live?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical meaning of רבי תנחום's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'יְשַׁלֵּשׁ אָדָם שְׁנוֹתָיו': dividing one's years into thirds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dividing a lifetime into thirds requires knowing its length, which no one knows.

steps.title: The division is done within each day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the three-way split means each day, not one's whole life.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we said this, we meant days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the division into thirds is done every day: part of each day for מקרא, part for משנה, and part for תלמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שנותיו' is explained as the person's time in general, measured day by day. This keeps רבי תנחום's teaching but changes the unit of time from a lifetime to a single day. Each day then has all three kinds of learning.

keyTerms.meaning: when we said it, what we meant was

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture this as 'first study only תנ״ך for years, then only משנה'. The גמרא means every single day includes all three.

phrases.english: When we said it, we meant days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording: 'years' means one's days.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the division is across a whole lifetime.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each day should be divided among מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי תנחום's rule means splitting each day's learning into three parts: מקרא, משנה, and תלמוד.

steps.title: Learning that bears fruit, and learning that does not
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the next words of the פסוק: if a person's learning produces fruit, his leaf will not wither; if not, both the student and the teacher are compared to the רשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That gives its fruit in its season.' רבא said: If it gives its fruit in its season, then 'its leaf will not wither.' But if not, then about both the learner and the teacher the פסוק says: 'Not so the wicked, but they are like chaff…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the פסוק. רבא says that learning which leads to proper results lasts. Learning that does not is compared to the next פסוק about the רשעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the פסוק as a condition: the 'leaf does not wither' only when the tree 'gives its fruit in its season'. Learning has to produce fruit, meaning it should lead to right action. If it does not, the very next פסוק, 'לא כן הרשעים', applies to both the one learning and the one teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: gives its fruit in its season
and its leaf will not wither
the one who learns, the student

phrases.english: "That gives its fruit in its season":
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:3

phrases.english: Rava said:
If "it gives its fruit in its season,"
then "its leaf will not wither."
But if not,
about the learner and about the teacher
about them the verse says:
"Not so the wicked, but [they are like chaff that the wind drives away]."
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:4. The גמרא quotes only the start, and 'וגו׳' means 'and so on'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק in תהלים, now its next words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah learning must bear fruit. Otherwise, both student and teacher fall under 'לא כן הרשעים'.

steps.title: Two mistakes: ruling too early and refusing to rule
steps.stepSummary: רב reads a פסוק in משלי as describing two harmful students: one who rules before he is qualified, and one who is qualified but refuses to rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא in the name of רב: What does the פסוק mean, 'For she has cast down many wounded'? This is a student who has not reached the level to rule, yet rules. 'And mighty are all her slain': this is a student who has reached the level to rule, yet does not rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains a פסוק in משלי as a warning about deciding הלכה. Two kinds of students cause harm: one rules too soon, and the other holds back when he should rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half, 'רבים חללים הפילה', describes a student who rules before he is ready, and his wrong rulings harm people. The second half, 'ועצומים כל הרוגיה', describes a capable ('mighty') student who refuses to rule, and people lose out because they never get the guidance he could give. Both acting too early and holding back too much are faults.

keyTerms.meaning: she cast down; can also mean 'miscarried'
reached the level to decide הלכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets two limits for a תלמיד חכם: do not rule on הלכה before you are qualified, and do not refuse to rule once you are.
steps.whatToRemember: Ruling on הלכה too early is harmful, and so is holding back from ruling once you are qualified.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"For she has cast down many wounded"?
phrases.notes: משלי 7:26. 'הפילה' can also mean a birth that comes too early, like a student ruling before his time.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה תַּלְמִיד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לְהוֹרָאָה וּמוֹרֶה,
phrases.english: This is a student who has not reached the level of ruling, yet rules;
"And mighty are all her slain":

phrases.aramaic: זֶה תַּלְמִיד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְהוֹרָאָה וְאֵינוֹ מוֹרֶה.
phrases.english: this is a student who has reached the level of ruling, yet does not rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on a פסוק from משלי, still on the theme of how a student uses his Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student who rules before he is qualified, and a qualified student who refuses to rule, both cause harm.

steps.title: Until what age is a student not ready to rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a student is considered too young to give halachic rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And until when?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's student who rules before he is ready (step 6) and asks how long that stage lasts. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a student who rules before he is qualified does harm. That raises a practical question: at what point does he become qualified? The גמרא asks for a clear limit.

phrases.english: And until when?
phrases.notes: He means: until what age is someone still the student who is 'not yet ready to rule' from step 6?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time limit of the 'not yet qualified' student that רב described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age at which a student may begin giving rulings.

steps.title: Until forty years old
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a student is considered not yet ready to rule until age forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until forty years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. Until a person turns forty, he should not give rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty is given as the age of full maturity in learning. Before forty, ruling counts as ruling 'before his time.'

phrases.english: Until forty years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A student should not rule until he reaches forty.

steps.title: But רבא gave rulings before forty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the forty-year rule from רבא, who gave rulings at a younger age.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא gave rulings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule it just gave. The great sage רבא ruled on הלכה before he was forty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ruling before forty were wrong, רבא would not have done it. His practice seems to go against the forty-year limit.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But Rava issued rulings!
phrases.notes: He means רבא ruled while still under forty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one may not rule before age forty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known case of a great sage, רבא, ruling before forty goes against the rule.

steps.title: רבא was equal to the leading scholar
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the forty-year limit does not apply to someone equal in knowledge to the leading scholar of his place, like רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they were equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבא's case was different because he was already equal to the top scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forty-year rule is the normal limit. It does not apply to someone whose knowledge already matches the greatest scholar around him. רבא was that kind of person, so he could rule early.
steps.whatToRemember: A student should not rule before forty. If he is already equal to the leading scholar, he may rule even earlier, as רבא did.

phrases.english: There, it is where they are equal.
phrases.notes: He means רבא was equal in knowledge to the greatest scholar of his town, so the age limit did not apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבא in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forty-year rule applies to everyone, so רבא's rulings look wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only to someone not yet equal to the leading scholar. רבא was equal.

steps.title: Even the everyday talk of Torah scholars is worth studying
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from 'its leaf does not wither' that even the ordinary conversation of תלמידי חכמים needs to be studied.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And its leaf does not wither.' רב אחא בר אדא said in the name of רב, and some say רב אחא בר אבא said in the name of רב המנונא in the name of רב: even the everyday conversation of Torah scholars needs study, as it says, 'And its leaf does not wither.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק in תהלים and explains the next words. רב teaches that even the small talk of a תלמיד חכם has value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the tree's fruit stood for real Torah learning (step 5). Here the leaves stand for the scholar's everyday talk. Leaves that never wither show that even this casual talk is lasting and worth learning from.

phrases.english: "And whose leaf does not wither":
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:3

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Adda said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: and some say Rav Aḥa bar Abba said
that Rav Hamnuna said that Rav said:
That even the ordinary conversation
of Torah scholars requires study,
as it is stated: "And whose leaf does not wither."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעָלֵהוּ לֹא יִבּוֹל, אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of ruling and returns to explaining the words of the פסוק in תהלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the casual speech of תלמידי חכמים is worth studying, learned from 'its leaf does not wither.'

steps.title: One who learns Torah succeeds with his property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that one who is busy with תורה will succeed in his property. He says this idea appears in the תורה, the נביאים, and the כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And whatever he does will succeed.' רבי יהושע בן לוי said: this idea is written in the תורה, repeated in the נביאים, and said a third time in the כתובים: whoever is busy with תורה, his property succeeds for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last words of the פסוק. רבי יהושע בן לוי says Torah learning brings success in a person's property and business, and he promises three sources for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step states the idea and announces that there are three sources. The next three steps bring each source in order: תורה, נביאים, כתובים.

keyTerms.meaning: Repeated (said a second time) in the Prophets
Said a third time in the Writings
One who is busy with Torah study

phrases.english: "And in whatever he does he shall prosper":
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:3, the last words of the same פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
This matter is written in the Torah,
and repeated in the Prophets,
and stated a third time in the Writings:
Whoever engages in Torah,
his property succeeds for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה יַצְלִיחַ, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who is busy with תורה succeeds in his property. This idea is found in all three parts of תנ״ך.

steps.title: The source in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The first source, from ספר דברים: keep the covenant so that you succeed in all you do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Written in the תורה, as it says: 'Keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you will succeed in all that you do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first of the three promised sources, from the תורה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties keeping the תורה to success in 'all that you do.' That is the same idea as 'whatever he does will succeed.'

phrases.english: It is written in the Torah, as it is written:
"Observe the words of this covenant
phrases.notes: דברים 29:8

phrases.english: and do them,

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעַן תַּשְׂכִּילוּ אֵת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּן״.
phrases.english: so that you may prosper in all that you do."
phrases.notes: Here תשכילו means 'succeed,' not 'become wise.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the first of the three sources promised in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: Torah study brings success in a person's affairs.

steps.title: The source in the נביאים
steps.stepSummary: The second source, from ספר יהושע: keep the Torah in your mouth day and night, and then you will succeed in your ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Repeated in the נביאים, as it says: 'This book of the Torah shall not leave your mouth, and you shall think about it day and night, so that you will keep everything written in it. For then you will succeed in your ways, and then you will prosper.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second source, from the נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק speaks openly about constant Torah study, 'day and night,' and promises success in return. It fits רבי יהושע בן לוי's words 'whoever is busy with תורה' very closely.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall not leave, shall not move away
And you shall think about it, go over it

phrases.english: It is repeated in the Prophets, as it is written:
"This book of the Torah shall not leave your mouth,
phrases.notes: יהושע 1:8. The word in square brackets fills in the full wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: and you shall meditate on it day and night,

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעַן תִּשְׁמֹר לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכׇל הַכָּתוּב בּוֹ
phrases.english: so that you take care to do all that is written in it;
for then you will make your ways prosper,
and then you will succeed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second of the three sources.
steps.raayaObject: Torah study brings success in a person's affairs.

steps.title: The source in the כתובים: back to our פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The third source is the very פסוק from תהלים that the גמרא has been explaining all along.
steps.simpleTranslation: Said a third time in the כתובים, as it says: 'But his desire is in the Torah of ה׳, and in His Torah he thinks day and night. He will be like a tree planted by streams of water, which gives its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither, and whatever he does will succeed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the third source, from the כתובים. This source is the same פסוק in תהלים it has been explaining, so the discussion comes full circle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins delight in תורה and learning 'day and night' with the promise that 'whatever he does will succeed.' So all three parts of תנ״ך teach the same lesson: success comes from Torah study.

keyTerms.meaning: He thinks about it, goes over it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי shows from the תורה, the נביאים, and the כתובים that one who is busy with Torah study succeeds in his affairs. The third source is the same פסוק in תהלים the whole sugya has been explaining.

phrases.english: It is stated a third time in the Writings, as it is written:
"But his delight is in the Torah of the Lord,
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:2–3, the same פסוק the גמרא has been explaining

phrases.english: and in His Torah he meditates day and night.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה כְּעֵץ שָׁתוּל עַל פַּלְגֵי מָיִם
phrases.english: And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water,
that gives its fruit in its season,
and whose leaf does not wither,
and in whatever he does he shall prosper."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the third and last source, completing רבי יהושע בן לוי's three proofs.
steps.raayaObject: Torah study brings success in a person's affairs.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three parts of תנ״ך agree that one who is busy with Torah study succeeds in what he does.

steps.title: Rabbi Alexandri sells 'life'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי calls out like a merchant, 'Who wants life?' When a crowd gathers, he quotes the פסוק in תהלים: guard your tongue from evil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי would call out: 'Who wants life? Who wants life?' Everyone gathered and came to him and said, 'Give us life!' He told them the פסוק: 'Who is the man who desires life… guard your tongue from evil…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רבי אלכסנדרי acts like a peddler selling goods, but the 'product' he offers is a פסוק about how to get real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People expected some special secret. His answer is simple: the way to life is guarding your speech. He quotes a new פסוק, from תהלים פרק לד rather than the תהלים פרק א the גמרא was just explaining, but it carries on the theme that living by the פסוקים brings blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: calls out, announces publicly (like a seller in the market)

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri would call out:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן בָּעֵי חַיֵּי? מַאן בָּעֵי חַיֵּי?
phrases.english: Who wants life? Who wants life?
Everyone gathered and came to him,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the word in square brackets. Both mean 'they gathered'.

phrases.english: They said to him: Give us life!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: ״מִי הָאִישׁ הֶחָפֵץ חַיִּים וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: He said to them: "Who is the man who desires life, etc.
phrases.notes: תהלים 34:13

phrases.english: Guard your tongue from evil, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 34:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the אגדה teachings about the rewards of תורה and good conduct.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The way to true life is guarding one's tongue from evil speech.

steps.title: Avoiding evil is not enough, you must also do good
steps.stepSummary: The next words of the פסוק, 'turn from evil and do good', teach that someone who only avoids bad speech cannot just go to sleep. He must actively do good.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Turn from evil and do good…' Perhaps a person will say: 'I guarded my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit, so I'll go and enjoy sleeping.' That is why the פסוק says: 'Turn from evil AND do good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק adds 'and do good' after 'turn from evil'. It is blocking a wrong idea a person might have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that doing nothing wrong is enough, so he can just rest. The words 'do good' teach that a person also has to take positive action.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps a person will say (introduces a mistaken idea)
indulge in sleep, spend my time sleeping
therefore the פסוק says (to teach otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Turn from evil' and 'do good' are not the same instruction said twice. The second half adds a separate duty: actively doing good.

phrases.english: "Turn from evil and do good, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 34:15

phrases.english: Perhaps a person will say: I guarded my tongue from evil
and my lips from speaking deceit,
so I will go and indulge in sleep?
Therefore the verse says: "Turn from evil and do good,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same chapter of תהלים that רבי אלכסנדרי quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoiding sin is not enough; one must also actively do good.

steps.title: 'Good' means תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from משלי that the 'good' a person must do is learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'good' means only תורה, as it says: 'For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My תורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which 'good' the פסוק means and brings a פסוק from משלי as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In משלי, תורה is called 'a good teaching'. So 'do good' in תהלים means learning תורה. Instead of sleeping, the person who guards his tongue should fill his time with תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: Guarding your speech brings life, but you also need to do good, and that 'good' is learning תורה.

phrases.english: And "good" means nothing other than Torah,
as it is stated: "For I have given you a good teaching;
phrases.notes: משלי 4:2

phrases.english: do not abandon My Torah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies what the 'good' from the previous step is.
steps.raayaObject: That 'do good' in תהלים means learning תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 4:2, which calls תורה 'a good teaching'

steps.title: Back to the משנה: wages for building the dome
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: a Jew helping gentiles build a bathhouse must stop at the כיפה, where idols are placed. רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוחנן says that if he built it anyway, his wages are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Once he reaches the dome, the place where they set up עבודה זרה, he may not build.' רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If he did build it, his pay is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה is over, and the גמרא returns to the משנה. It quotes a line from the משנה and brings a ruling about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says building the dome is not allowed from the start. רבי יוחנן adds what happens after the fact: if the Jew built it, he may still keep and use his wages.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying you may build the dome from the start. He only says that after the fact the pay is not forbidden.

phrases.english: Once he reaches the dome,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about a Jew helping gentiles build a bathhouse.

phrases.english: the place where they set up idol worship [he may not build it].

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If he did build it, his wages are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the הלכה of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a Jew built the dome where idols are placed, his wages are permitted after the fact.

steps.title: Why say it? The dome is only an accessory
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say this. The dome is only an accessory to idol worship, and accessories are not forbidden until they are actually used for worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious? The dome is only an accessory of עבודה זרה. Accessories of עבודה זרה, according to both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, are not forbidden until they are used for the worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling, saying it is too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newly built dome has not been used for worship yet. Both תנאים agree that an accessory only becomes forbidden once it has been used. So obviously the builder's pay is fine, and the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious! (a challenge that a statement is unnecessary)
accessories that serve idol worship, not the idol itself
until they are used for the worship

phrases.english: That is obvious!
They are accessories of idol worship,
and accessories of idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֵּין לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: both according to Rabbi Yishmael and according to Rabbi Akiva,
are not forbidden until they are used for worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 19 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement in the name of רבי יוחנן that the wages are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The dome is only an accessory, and accessories are forbidden only after being used. So the ruling seems obvious.

steps.title: The ruling is about building the idol itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the ruling is needed for a Jew who built the actual idol, not just the dome.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: The ruling was only needed for the idol itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the 'it's obvious' challenge by moving the ruling to a harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a Jew made an actual idol for a gentile, you might think his pay is forbidden. רבי יוחנן teaches that even then the wages are permitted, because the idol has not yet been worshipped. That is a real new teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed only for (this case)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.english: It was needed only for the idol itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case the ruling refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to be about the dome, which is only an accessory, so it was obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is about a Jew who built the idol itself, and even then his wages are permitted.

steps.title: What about the view that a gentile's idol is forbidden right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי ירמיה's answer works only for the view that a gentile's idol is forbidden after it is worshipped. According to the view that it is forbidden right away, the wages should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says: an idol made by a Jew is forbidden right away, but a gentile's idol is forbidden only once it is worshipped. But according to the one who says a gentile's idol is also forbidden right away, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה's answer. This step sets up a problem, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about when a gentile's idol becomes forbidden. If it is forbidden only after worship, the builder's pay is fine, since the idol was never worshipped. If it is forbidden as soon as it is made, then the builder made something forbidden, and it is hard to see how his wages could be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: this works out well for the one who says
forbidden immediately, as soon as it is made
what can be said? (the answer is a problem)

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate views are compared here. The question is not whether a Jew's idol is forbidden right away, since both agree it is. The argument is only about a gentile's idol.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲסוּרָה מִיָּד,
phrases.english: An idol of a Jew is forbidden immediately,
and that of a gentile only once it is worshipped; that is fine,
phrases.notes: Here the idol was built for a gentile and not yet worshipped, so the pay is fine.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: שֶׁל גּוֹי אֲסוּרָה מִיָּד,
phrases.english: but according to the one who says that a gentile's idol is forbidden immediately,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's answer from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's explanation that the wages for building the idol itself are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a gentile's idol is forbidden as soon as it is made, then the builder produced a forbidden object, and his wages should be forbidden.

steps.title: The ruling is needed only for the final hammer stroke
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא explains that רבי יוחנן's ruling works even for the view that a gentile's idol is forbidden right away. The object only becomes an idol at the final stroke, and that last stroke is worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר עולא said: The ruling was needed only for the last hammer stroke. What makes something an idol? Finishing the work. When is the work finished? With the last stroke. And the last stroke alone is not worth even a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רבי ירמיה's answer and gives a new one. רבה בר עולא shows why the wages are permitted even for the view that an idol is forbidden as soon as it is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The object becomes an idol only when it is finished, and it is finished only with the very last stroke. All the earlier work was done on something that was not yet an idol. The only pay connected to the idol is for that last stroke, and it is worth less than a פרוטה, so it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The final hammer stroke that finishes the work
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount of money that counts in הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: The worker is not being paid only for the last stroke. He is paid for all his work, but only the last stroke happens when the object becomes an idol.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Ulla said:
phrases.notes: "Rather" tells us the גמרא is setting aside רבי ירמיה's answer from Step 21.

phrases.english: It was needed only for the final hammer stroke.

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מַאן קָא גָרֵים לַהּ?
phrases.english: An idol, what causes it to become one?
The completion of the work,
and when is the work completed?
With the final stroke.

phrases.aramaic: מַכּוֹשׁ אַחֲרוֹן לֵית בֵּיהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה.
phrases.english: The final stroke is not worth a perutah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22 by replacing רבי ירמיה's answer with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the ruling refers to the moment the idol is finished
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the idol is forbidden as soon as it is made, all the wages for making it should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The object becomes an idol only with the final stroke. That stroke is worth less than a פרוטה, so the wages are permitted even according to that view.

steps.title: Wages build up from the start of the job to the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this ruling assumes a worker earns his wage step by step during the whole job, not all at once at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that he holds that wages are earned from the beginning to the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the basic idea that רבה בר עולא's answer depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wages were earned only when the job was finished, the whole payment would come at the moment the object becomes an idol, and it would be forbidden. The answer works only because pay is earned bit by bit during the work. So most of the pay was earned before the object was an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: We see, so it turns out
From the beginning to the end

steps.whatToRemember: An object becomes an idol only when the work is finished. Since wages build up during the whole job, the worker's pay for making it is permitted.

phrases.english: Evidently he holds,
phrases.notes: "He" means the one who said the wages are permitted: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: that wages are earned from the beginning to the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the principle that Step 23's answer relies on.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A worker's wage builds up throughout the job, so pay for work done before the object became an idol is permitted.

steps.title: New משנה: jewelry for idols and selling attached produce to gentiles
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids making jewelry for idols, but רבי אליעזר permits it when done for pay. It also forbids selling things attached to the ground to gentiles. They may be sold once cut, and רבי יהודה allows selling them on condition that they are cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not make jewelry for an idol, such as necklaces, nose rings and rings. רבי אליעזר says: For pay, it is permitted. One may not sell them things attached to the ground, but one may sell once it is cut. רבי יהודה says: One may sell on condition that it be cut.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two separate rules. The first is about making jewelry for idols, and the second is about selling things still attached to the ground to gentiles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids making idol jewelry in all cases, while רבי אליעזר permits it if it is done for wages. For attached things such as trees or crops, the תנא קמא requires that they already be cut before the sale. רבי יהודה says it is enough to sell them on condition that they will be cut.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached to the ground, like a growing tree or crop
On condition that it be cut

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And one may not make jewelry for an idol,
necklaces, nose rings and rings.
Rabbi Eliezer says: For payment, it is permitted.
One may not sell them anything attached to the ground,
phrases.notes: "Them" means gentiles. The משנה is going back to its earlier topic of selling to them.

phrases.english: but he may sell it once it is cut.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He may sell it on condition that it be cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the previous discussion and opens a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making jewelry for idols is forbidden, though רבי אליעזר permits it for pay. Selling attached things to gentiles is forbidden until they are cut, though רבי יהודה permits selling on condition that they be cut.

steps.title: What is the source for not selling attached things?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule against selling things attached to the ground to gentiles. רבי יוסי בר חנינא is about to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things? רבי יוסי בר חנינא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from. It is setting up an answer from רבי יוסי בר חנינא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is aimed at the משנה's last rule, that one may not sell attached things to gentiles. Only the name of the one answering appears here. His actual source comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: This is asking about the rule against selling attached things to gentiles.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule in Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that one may not sell things attached to the ground to gentiles.
